supported_os: Other CentOS/RHEL-like systems supported by the installer
django_workload.notes: Two-machine deployment is recommended: Cassandra database server plus Django server/client. Standalone mode is supported. Recommended network latency between machines is 0.1-0.15 ms. The database address is supplied at run time.

supported_os: CentOS/RHEL-like systems supported by the installer
feedsim.notes: The autoscale job creates approximately one workload instance per 100 CPU cores. CPU boost is recommended. The target is maximum QPS while maintaining p95 latency at or below 500 ms.

health_check.notes: Network tests require client or auxiliary machines. The workload measures memory bandwidth/latency, network latency/bandwidth, and nanosleep scheduling overhead.

required_user_files: HHVM 3.30 binary package or locally built HHVM 3.30 installation
mediawiki.notes: HHVM 3.30 is required. SELinux must be disabled. MariaDB and nginx are installed/configured. CPU boost is relevant for high-core-count runs. The default load generator is wrk.

required_user_files: NVMe storage setup mounted at the configured Spark data path
supported_os: Ubuntu systems supported by the installer
spark_standalone.notes: The documented distributed setup requires one compute node and one or more storage nodes. Recommended storage-node resources are at least 26 cores and 64 GB RAM, at least 500 GB combined free storage, NVMe SSDs, and at least 50 Gbps aggregate network bandwidth. NVMe-over-TCP kernel support and IOMMU passthrough configuration may be required.

supported_os: Ubuntu systems supported by the installer
tao_bench.notes: CentOS Stream 8 with Linux 5.19 is recommended. Three machines are recommended: one server and two clients. Recommended network latency is 0.1-0.15 ms, with at least 10 Gbps for systems up to 72 logical cores and 20 Gbps above 72 logical cores. IOMMU passthrough is required when IOMMU is enabled.

video_transcode_bench.notes: The installer builds FFmpeg and the SVT-AV1, AOM, x264, and VMAF dependencies. CPU boost is recommended. The dataset requires manual download because the source site requires registration.

wdl_bench.notes: WDLBench contains folly, lzbench, OpenSSL, and fbthrift-based workloads. Jobs support single-core, all-core, multi-threaded, individual folly benchmarks, compression, and crypto modes.
